identity: Politician and journalist · People's Republic of China · 1895–1928
title: Xiang Jingyu's birth chart
metaDescription: Xiang Jingyu's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 11.4° Virgo. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Across the ten placements whose signs are settled, mutable leads with six. Mutable weight bends without breaking — the chart of translators, editors, and second drafts.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: At noon on that date the Sun stood at 11.4° Virgo, inside the second decan (10°–20°), whose traditional sub-ruler is Saturn. The decan is the older, finer division — it is what the sign looks like once you stop rounding it to thirty degrees.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: The personal planets sit Mercury at 26.4° Virgo, Venus at 3.3° Libra, Mars at 23.5° Virgo. Mercury in an earth sign reads as thought with its feet on the ground; Venus in an air sign reads as attraction that begins as conversation; Mars in an earth sign reads as effort banked steadily until it tells.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Nothing in the geometry sits closer than the Sun and Pluto: 1.4° from an exact square. Nothing in a square flows; everything in it works. The old texts kept squares for the charts they respected. Behind it, Mercury conjunction Mars at 2.9°, and Venus sextile Jupiter at 3.4° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. All of it stands whatever the hour was: each angle was tested from midnight to midnight before it was written down.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: The Sun opposes the Moon while both square Pluto. The t-square is the figure the old texts trusted for output: friction with a fixed address. Uranus makes no major aspect that survives the day; the old reading gives such a planet autonomy — it acts alone, sometimes loudly.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The dignity table, which predates the outer planets and only ever spoke for seven, marks three placements here. Mercury in Virgo at 26.4° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Venus in Libra at 3.3° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Jupiter in Cancer at 29.9° is in exaltation. Dignity is a statement about conditions, not about worth.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Counting only the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the chart runs 4 water, 3 earth, 3 air by element and 6 mutable, 2 cardinal, 2 fixed by modality. A water emphasis reads as porousness: the room is registered whole, long before it is analysed in parts. No settled placement falls in fire — an absence the tradition treats as information, not as a defect. Venus was retrograde — the optical reversal the tradition reads as review — energy turned over before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Pisces for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 11.8° between midnight and midnight. The missing clock moves the Moon by half a sign at most here, and the boundary was never close. At the noon reference it stands at 10.8°.
